title: The quiet room
bodyMd:
A fictional school converted a storage room into a reading area. After adding soft wall panels, the designers measured a shorter reverberation time: sounds faded more quickly. Teachers nevertheless reported that the room remained distracting during lessons in the adjacent music classroom. The panels reduced reflections within the reading room but did little to stop sound entering through a poorly sealed connecting door.

The team then improved the door seal and repeated both measurements and user observations. The episode showed why a favorable result for one acoustic property should not be treated as proof of overall quietness. Reverberation and sound transmission were related to the experience of the room, but they required different interventions. The team’s revised report named the property measured rather than using a single broad claim that the room had become “soundproof.”
